mcqs.question: For a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm, which object distance (in cm) will produce an image distance greater than 30 cm?
mcqs.explanation: Using the Cartesian sign convention, f = -15 cm (concave). Apply 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. For u = -12 cm: 1/v = -1/15 + 1/12 = ( -4 + 5 ) /60 = 1/60, so v = +60 cm, which is greater than 30 cm. The other choices give v ≤ 30 cm or a virtual image. Hence -12 cm is the correct object distance.

mcqs.question: A concave mirror forms a real, inverted image of a candle placed 30 cm in front of it. The image is 45 cm in front of the mirror. What is the focal length of the mirror?
mcqs.explanation: With Cartesian sign convention: u = -30 cm, v = -45 cm (real image on same side as object). Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u = -1/45 - 1/30 = -(2/90 + 3/90) = -5/90 = -1/18. Hence f = -18 cm, indicating a concave mirror. The other options do not satisfy the equation.

mcqs.question: A convex mirror has a focal length of +20 cm. An object is placed 40 cm in front of the mirror. Find the image distance (in cm).
mcqs.explanation: For a convex mirror, f = +20 cm and u = -40 cm. Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u: 1/20 = 1/v - 1/40 → 1/v = 1/20 + 1/40 = 3/40 → v = 40/3 ≈ 13.33 cm. Positive v indicates a virtual image behind the mirror. The other values are inconsistent with the formula.

mcqs.question: An object 5 cm tall is placed 15 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. What is the height of the image?
mcqs.explanation: Using sign convention: f = -10 cm, u = -15 cm. Mirror formula gives v = -30 cm (virtual, upright). Magnification m = v/u = (-30)/(-15) = 2. Image height = m × object height = 2 × 5 cm = 10 cm, upright. Option A matches this result.

mcqs.question: In mirror experiments, a magnification of –0.5 indicates that the image is:

options.A: Upright and half the size of the object
options.B: Inverted and half the size of the object
options.C: Upright and twice the size of the object
options.D: Inverted and twice the size of the object

mcqs.answer: Inverted and half the size of the object
mcqs.explanation: A negative magnification denotes an inverted image. The magnitude 0.5 means the image size is half that of the object. Therefore the correct interpretation is an inverted image half the size of the object.

mcqs.question: A concave mirror of focal length 12 cm forms an image that is twice the size of the object. Where is the object placed (distance from the mirror in cm)?
mcqs.explanation: For a real, inverted image twice the size, magnification m = –2. Using m = –v/u → v = 2u. Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u = 1/(2u) + 1/u = 3/(2u). Hence u = 3f/2 = 3×12/2 = 18 cm. The object distance is 18 cm in front of the mirror (u = –18 cm). Option A is correct.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 25 cm in front of a convex mirror whose focal length is 20 cm. What is the nature and position of the image?

options.A: Virtual, erect, 11.1 cm behind the mirror
options.B: Real, inverted, 11.1 cm in front of the mirror
options.C: Virtual, erect, 40 cm behind the mirror
options.D: Real, inverted, 40 cm in front of the mirror

mcqs.answer: Virtual, erect, 11.1 cm behind the mirror
mcqs.explanation: For a convex mirror, f = +20 cm, u = -25 cm. Mirror formula: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/20 + 1/25 = (5+4)/100 = 9/100 → v = 100/9 ≈ 11.1 cm (positive, indicating a virtual image behind the mirror). Convex mirrors always produce erect, reduced images. Hence option A is correct.

mcqs.question: A student places a candle 40 cm in front of a concave mirror and obtains a real image 20 cm in front of the mirror. Using the Cartesian sign convention, what is the sign of the focal length of the mirror?
mcqs.explanation: For a concave mirror, the focal length is taken as negative in the Cartesian sign convention. The given data (real image in front of the mirror) confirms the mirror is concave, so f is negative. Therefore option B is correct; the other options do not follow the convention.
